annual_values: Each row is one canonical financial metric for one company and fiscal year, as originally reported in that year's 10-K. Key columns: `cik` (join to companies), `metric` (such as 'revenue', 'net_income', 'operating_income', 'capital_expenditure', 'operating_cash_flow', 'total_assets', 'inventory'; the metrics table lists all 28), `fiscal_year` (the company's own label, so Walmart's year ending January 2024 is 2024 but Ulta's year ending January 2024 is 2023), `value` and `unit` ('USD' in dollars, not millions; 'USD/shares' for EPS; 'shares'), `period_start` and `period_end` (period_start is NULL for balance-sheet items, which are measured at the year end), `tag` (the XBRL tag the value came from) and `latest_value` (the figure in the most recent filing for the same period, which differs when the company restated it). This is the main table for reported figures, ratios, growth rates, multi-year averages and comparisons between companies. Divide value by 1e6 for millions or 1e9 for billions.
companies: Each row is one company, identified by its SEC Central Index Key `cik`. Columns: `ticker` (NULL for companies that no longer trade, such as Activision Blizzard and Foot Locker), `name` (the short name used in questions, such as 'Coca-Cola' or 'JPMorgan'), `sec_name` (SEC's registered name), `sector` (GICS sector, such as 'Information Technology') and `fiscal_year_end` (month and day of the latest fiscal year end, as MMDD). Join every other table on `cik`. Use it to find a company by name or ticker and for questions about sectors.
concepts: Each row describes one XBRL concept: `taxonomy` (usually 'us-gaap'), `tag` (such as 'PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment'), a readable `label` and SEC's `description`. Join to facts on taxonomy and tag to find the tag behind a line item that annual_values doesn't cover.
facts: Each row is one XBRL fact as reported in one 10-K or 10-Q: `cik`, `taxonomy`, `tag`, `unit`, the period (`period_start`, NULL for balance-sheet instants, and `period_end`), `value`, and the filing it came from (`accn`, `form`, `filed`, `fiscal_year` and `fiscal_period` as SEC labels the filing). A figure reported in several filings appears once per filing, and comparatives appear in later filings too. Use it for items annual_values doesn't cover and for quarterly figures; for annual metrics, prefer annual_values.
filings: Each row is one 10-K, 10-K/A, 10-KT or 10-Q filing: accession number `accn`, `cik`, `form`, filing date `filed`, `fiscal_year` (for annual reports, the company's own label; for quarterly reports, SEC's), `fiscal_period` ('FY', 'Q1', 'Q2' or 'Q3'), `period_end` (the last day of the period the report covers) and `sec_fiscal_year` (SEC's label, kept for reference). Join to facts and annual_values on `accn`.
metric_tags: Each row is one XBRL tag that can supply a canonical metric, with its `priority` (1 is tried first; a lower-priority tag is used only in years when no higher one is reported). Use it to explain where a metric's values come from.
metrics: Each row defines one canonical metric used in annual_values: `metric` (its name), `label`, `description`, `kind` ('duration' for income and cash-flow items covering a fiscal year; 'instant' for balance-sheet items at the year end), `unit`, `statement` ('income statement', 'cash flow statement' or 'balance sheet') and `pick` ('priority' to use the first tag reported in metric_tags order, 'largest' to take the largest figure among the tags, as revenue does). Use it to see which metrics exist and what each one means.
